additionalCoursework:
For applicants to the Ponce (Main) Campus only, three (3) Spanish credits are required because PHSU’s partner hospitals and clinics in Ponce serve a predominantly Spanish-speaking population.

In addition to the above requirements, we strongly recommend coursework in biochemistry, cellular biology, microbiology, genetics, and statistics, as well as Liberal Arts and/or Humanities.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: PHSU is committed to recruiting and retaining qualified students, regardless of being disadvantaged or underrepresented, as long as they meet all the requisites established by the Institution.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: The student must request from the regristars office an LoA at least 30 days prior to the LoA commencement date, unless medical circumstances require immediate authorization (e.g., automobile accidente).  A personal or medical leave may be authorized when a student is experiencing complying personal and medical circumstances that are temporarily affecting his/her academic progress.  The student must submitt a physicians note certifiying the medical problem or reason.  The total time of leave cannot exceed 180 days within a 12 months period.  A studen who fails to return after an authorized an LoA will be academically withdrawn and an R2T4 calculation will be performed and subsequently an exit counseling instructional letter will be sent to the student.

medSchoolStudLife.setting:
The Ponce campus is located in  the city of Ponce, PR at the Zona Industrial Reparada on Route #2 .  basic sciences courses are taught in the Academic Building next to our library and across the Research building.  Our clinical years are held in affiliated hospitals, healthcare facilities and outpatient clinics.  The institution also owns an outpatient clinic (Wellness Center) and several behavioral health centers.  The affiliation networks provide about 2,000 beds and several ambulatory facilities available for clinical teaching and training.  

Our St. Louis campus is located in Downtown west next to the newly constructed Citypark where the discoveries are endless in the big city with a small town feel. St. Louis offers attractions in culture, arts, outdoors, medical and tech industries, and memorable architecture. With affordable housing and close-knit communities, St. Louis is the ideal place for students to advance toward their dream careers.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: On-campus housing is not available. The university does maintain a list of affordable apartments within a 10-mile radius. Rental prices vary by location.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: LGBTQ+ Support Groups in addition to counseling services.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: As part of activities related to the well-being of our students, we carry out an initial integration into the academic community through the orientation period. The Vice Presidency of Student Affairs carries out special events such as karaoke, yoga, Zumba, arts, workouts, sports tournaments, self-care, expo health events, nutrition, and personal training workshops. In addition, the creation of interest groups and student organizations is actively promoted to have extracurricular activities that strengthen the emotional and intellectual part of the student.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
At Ponce Health Sciences University (PHSU), our campuses in Ponce, Puerto Rico, and St. Louis, Missouri, reflect a unique multicultural identity. We take pride in fostering an inclusive environment where students, faculty, and staff from diverse backgrounds come together to share their perspectives and experiences. This cultural richness not only enhances the learning experience but also prepares future physicians to excel in diverse healthcare settings.

Our bilingual campus culture in Ponce, PR, embraces both English and Spanish, encouraging cultural exchange and global perspectives. As a Latino-led institution, we are deeply connected to the communities we serve, offering students the opportunity to address real-world healthcare challenges in urban, tropical, and multicultural contexts. At PHSU, diversity is not just celebrated—it’s central to our mission of creating compassionate and culturally competent healthcare leaders.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Professional and business casual on a case/case basis.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Students must contact each location's Academic Affairs and Student Affairs offices for details and availability.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Commences with community medicine during the first year and continues into subsequent years.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Classes utilize the flipped classroom method in addition to small group discussions.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical rotations start at the onset of the 3rd year in various locations.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: PHSU’s MD program is an LCME accredited, culturally-focused 4-year program providing students with an ethnically-diverse, innovative and tech-driven education in a variety of medical practices. The first two academic years provide a pre-clinical foundation with core disciplines as well as an introduction to clinical skills, behavioral science, and medical ethics. Our interactive and innovative curriculum helps prepare students for clinical rotations in core specialties during their third and fourth years. With an additional five months of advanced specialty elective rotations, students graduate with a culturally competent and high-impact degree, ready to serve communities in need.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: PHSU was founded to provide primary care physicians, particularly for the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.  Interdisciplinary community medicine courses are required from year one.   These courses involve the three-primary care disciplines: Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, and Pediatrics.  They have a didactic component focusing on community medicine; geriatric/gerontology concepts and an experiential component. Subsequently, disciplines have evolved, and medical graduates also train in customized specialties, such as surgery, internal medicine, pediatrics, ob/gyn.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
Ponce Health Sciences University (PHSU) is accredited by the Liaison Committee on Medical Education (LCME), with more than 48 years of experience providing high-quality education, research, and health services in the fields of medicine, biological sciences, psychology, public health, nursing and now dentistry. 

Our medical program is available in Ponce, PR and St. Louis, MO. Students can complete their clinical rotations in diverse settings, from rural clinics to tertiary-care hospitals in Puerto Rico and the USA.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The mission of the School of Medicine is to educate ethical professionals who provide compassionate, culturally competent healthcare and generate high impact research to reduce health disparities in the populations we serve in Puerto Rico and the U.S., through high-quality education in a diverse environment.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Letters must be submitted through AMCAS.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: The Admissions Committee requires three recommendation letters:  two from professors and one from an individual familiar with the applicant’s skills and abilities are preferred. A premedical committee letter is also accepted in lieu of the three letters.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
Interviews are conducted virtually in the Multiple Mini Interview format to support a holistic admissions process and evaluate premedical competencies that align with PHSU-SOM’s mission to train ethical professionals who provide compassionate, culturally competent health care and generate high impact research to reduce health disparities in the populations we serve in Puerto Rico and the US. There are live and asynchronous interviews.

Interviews will be conducted in Spanish and English for applicants applying to the Main Campus (Ponce) and in English only for applicants applying to the St. Louis Campus.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Yes, interviews will be held live and asynchronously.

medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: Our admissions committee considers the scores of the first three MCAT attempts, taken within the past five (5) years.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: A minumum MCAT of 494 is required, within first three (3) attemps, taken within the past five (5) years.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: A minimum AMCAS cumulative and science GPA of 2.70 is required for evaluation.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Advanced Placement credits should be recorded in the college transcript.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Candidates for the doctoral medical program who are in an alternate/waitlisted status can submit a letter of interest to the admissions staff and the committee. These are presented to the Admissions Committee as part of the student's profile.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Ponce Health Sciences University (PHSU) intends for its MD program graduates to become highly skilled and competent doctors who can provide compassionate, culturally competent health care in accordance with its mission, who can satisfy PHSU-SOM academic and performance requirements, and who are eligible for graduate medical education and medical licensure. All candidates accepted to the MD Program in the PHSU School of Medicine must be able to meet the school’s technical standards. Candidates are asked to review the standards and sign a form certifying that they have read and understood them and can meet them with or without reasonable accommodation. Reasonable accommodations are available in accordance with PHSU’s Reasonable Accommodation Policy. However, candidates should be able to perform in a reasonably independent manner all skill levels described in the technical standards, which PHSU holds as mandatory for the safe and effective practice of medicine.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Students are admitted to Ponce Health Sciences University regardless of their financial circumstances and are invited to contact the  Financial Aid Office to seek further information. To learn more, please visit https://www.psm.edu/financial-aid-services/. Detailed information is available at https://www.psm.edu/consumer-information-and-student-achievement-guide/
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy:
1. Students must pay 100% of tuition at the time of registration. 
2. Students with an approved Financial Aid that covers a 100% of tuition and fees are authorized to register. 
3. Students with approved Financial Aid less than 100% of tuition and fees, must pay the pending balance upon registration.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail:
Beginning February 19th of each academic year, applicants holding one or more acceptance offers can select “Plan to Enroll” in the AMCAS application at any school from which they have received an acceptance offer. This allows the PHSU admissions team to view the number of applicants who selected our institution.
Applicants should use the tool to select “Commit to Enroll" on April 30th.

medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
When evaluating MD program applicants, the MD Admissions Committee aims to select the most competitive applicants with integrity, maturity, service orientation, as well as leadership, and enthusiasm for working with others. Through a holistic admissions process, the MD Admissions Committee evaluates applicants considering the following premedical competencies and attributes:

academic performance
commitment to a career in medicine
critical thinking
cultural competency
ethical responsibility
humanism
integrity and maturity
language and communication skills
leadership
resilience and adaptability
service orientation
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Premedical shadowing is strongly recommended. Shadowing is a crucial component of the holistic evaluation process for medical school candidates. It provides applicants with firsthand exposure to the realities of medical practice, helping them gain a deeper understanding of the profession and the challenges faced by healthcare providers. This experience allows candidates to demonstrate their commitment to pursuing medicine and their ability to empathize with patients. Furthermore, shadowing offers admissions committees valuable insight into an applicant’s motivation, maturity, and readiness for the demands of medical education.
